title: She Loves to Cook, and She Loves to Eat
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Yuki Nomoto, who loves to cook but has a small appetite, invites her neighbour Totoko Kasuga, who loves to eat, to share a large meal. Their friendship over food slowly becomes romance; Nomoto realises she is a lesbian with advice from an asexual online friend, Kasuga has cut ties with a family that served women smaller portions than men, and a new neighbour begins therapy for a fear of eating in public (Wikipedia).
life_message: Sharing food and honest company lets people become who they are, free of others' ideas of what is 'normal'.

content.note: Slow romance between two women; no explicit content noted (Wikipedia, ANN via Wikipedia).
Kaname's phobia of eating in public from childhood trauma, now in cognitive therapy; estrangement from family (Wikipedia; MU Deipnophobia, AniList Estranged Family).
Live-action drama adaptation; food posting on social media.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Kasuga quietly cuts ties rather than confronting her father (Wikipedia).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Each woman leaves expectations of 'normal' behind (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Chosen neighbours replace family as the support network.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Male precedence in Kasuga's family is rejected (Wikipedia; MU Sexism).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Inherited family roles questioned; therapy valued.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Identity, tolerance and quality of life are central.

folkways.japan: Serving men larger portions and expecting women to marry reflect traditional Japanese household norms that the story questions; the josei format suits adult everyday life.

delivery.evidence: Reviewers cited on Wikipedia say cooking frames everyday sexism in the background and it reads as comfort food.

personified.ideology: traditional family order where men come first

delivery.note: Social critique is voiced through characters' experiences rather than lectures, though the father's view is presented only as a harm (to verify).

winners_losers: Nomoto, Kasuga, Yako and Kaname find acceptance and healing in their chosen circle; Kasuga's father's view that men come first is rejected, and she breaks with her family (Wikipedia).
to_verify: How Kasuga's family is drawn on page (summaries give only the father's view of women's place).
